TASK: REVISE ONE SECTION

You wrote section 5 of 6, "What the measurement cannot say", of the report "AI readiness of federal statistical publishers: what one measurement shows". It was checked, and it comes back to you once with the notes below. Rewrite the whole section so that the notes no longer apply, keeping its argument and keeping every fact you can keep under the rules.

WHAT THIS SECTION MUST DO: Say what this measurement cannot establish, each limit as precisely as a claim states it: findings that are errors rather than failures, and why; bodies that could not be ranked because they refused the client, which is itself a finding about access; how much a rank rests on a single check; candidate indicators that enter no count; indicators that are specified but not yet measured, and what blocks each kind; and how much of the framework's evidence carries a pinpoint locator.

NOTES
- The word 'bureau' (in some form) is used 9 times in this section; use it at most 5 times.
- The word 'check' (in some form) is used 6 times in this section; use it at most 5 times.
- The word 'rank' (in some form) is used 6 times in this section; use it at most 5 times.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'build mark measured' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [2, 5]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'bureau labor statistics' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [3, 5]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'bureau transportation statistics' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [3, 5]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'check definition surface' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [5, 6]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'few row finding' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [4, 5]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'indicator record mark' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [5, 6]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'mark measured specify' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [2, 5]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'office research evaluation' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [3, 5]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'record mark measure' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [5, 6]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'research evaluation statistics' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [3, 5]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'statistics office research' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [3, 5]; say it once and refer back.

SENTENCES ALREADY CUT (a checker found them unsupported, or a number in them was not in a claim they cite). Do not state these facts again in any wording; the claims do not support them.
- "Their absence from the ranking therefore records that no check could be judged on them, and it says nothing about the quality of their products." (checker: CL-050 says the three bodies have no scored leg with a judged row, not that no check could be judged on them; the impossibility and the inference about product quality are not stated.)
- "Its record holds 50 indicators, of which 48 belong to the framework and 2 are candidates, the check for access policy coherence and the check for discoverability from the product page, and a candidate enters no count until the operator adopts it." (checker: CL-046 says a candidate enters no framework count; the sentence drops the 'framework' qualifier and says it enters no count, which the 50-indicator record count including candidates contradicts.)
- "Of 50 indicator evidence cells, 10 carry a pinpoint locator, and of the 154 links that tie an indicator to its evidence, 34 point at a document with a locator." (checker: CL-054 says 34 of 154 edges point at a located document, not at a document with a locator; the sentence changes what the 34 edges point to.)

THE SECTION AS IT STANDS (markers in place)
The same distinction bounds the measurement as a whole, because a refused request shows only that the scanner was not served, not that the thing it sought is missing [c:CL-045, CL-038]. For the Census Bureau, the scanner, which identified itself and did not log in, met a refusal by the host or a disallow in robots.txt on 24 of the Bureau's 89 findings [c:CL-038]. Among the Bureau's 27 absences, moreover, 4 were judged only after some refused or disallowed probes had been set aside, so those verdicts rest on part of the evidence the checks would otherwise read [c:CL-038]. The limit is sharper still for three bodies, because of the 16 statistical bodies in the cycle only 13 are ranked, and the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Bureau of Transportation Statistics and the Office of Research, Evaluation, and Statistics have no scored check with a judged row [c:CL-050].

A rank can also rest on far less evidence than a body's full set of findings would suggest [c:CL-052, CL-053]. On the published matrices the Census Bureau has 18 failing of 39 judged rows, and those matrices carry fewer rows than the 89 findings the cycle holds for the Bureau, because they publish one row per check and surface [c:CL-052]. Under the hierarchical equal-weight score, however, the Bureau ranks 7 of 13 with a score of 0.143, and that rank turns on a single check, the check for a definitions surface, on which 0 of 2 judged rows passed [c:CL-053]. Were that one verdict reversed, the Bureau would rank 1, so a reader should take a rank as a statement about a few checks rather than about a body's readiness as a whole [c:CL-053].

The framework is also larger than the part of it this measurement scored [c:CL-046, CL-049]. Of the framework's 48 indicators, the record marks 23 as measured, 1 as having its measurement built but not yet marked measured, and 24 as specified only [c:CL-049]. What holds back the 25 indicators not marked measured differs by kind: 11 have no standard to measure against, 7 need the cooperation of agencies, 6 need open tooling, none is blocked by funding, and 1 is not blocked at all [c:CL-001]. Money, therefore, is not what stands between the specified indicators and a measurement of them [c:CL-001].

Finally, only part of the framework's evidence can be traced to an exact place in a source [c:CL-054]. Moreover, 16 indicators have no such link at all, and 84 of the 282 documents admitted to the record are cited by one [c:CL-054]. A reader can therefore confirm that a source stands behind much of the framework, but can find the exact passage behind an indicator in only 10 cases [c:CL-054].

REGISTER
- Technical and readable. The reader is a federal statistician or a manager at a statistical agency: expert in statistics, not in web crawling or AI.
- Each paragraph carries one thought, stated in its first sentence (the topic sentence); the rest of the paragraph develops it.
- In each sentence, put what the reader already knows first and what is new last, where the stress falls (Gopen and Swan, "The Science of Scientific Writing", 1990).
- Wherever the logic turns (a contrast, a cause, a consequence, an example), say so with a connective word: but, so, because, therefore, for example, however.
- Write whole sentences with a finite verb. Do not follow a long sentence with a short fragment or a short qualifying sentence (for example "Not a browser." or "Only the public pages."); fold the qualification into the sentence it qualifies. This pattern is measured and a section that repeats it fails.
- Vary sentence length naturally. Do not repeat a phrase you have already used; find the plain word for each thing and use it once where once is enough.
- Never use the em dash or the en dash. Never use these words: load-bearing, load bearing, hallucinate (or any form of it; say confabulate), delve, testament. Do not cite Gartner.
- Plain names, no codes. Name a statistical body by its name (the NAMES table gives it), never by a code such as CENSUS or BLS. Name a check by what it tests (for example "the check for a machine-readable licence"), never by a letter-and-number code such as D1 or B2. Do not use task codes, decision numbers, file names, file paths, field names in backticks, or words like harness, pipeline, record node, leg, route, cycle id; call the measuring client "the scanner". The one identifier you may write is the name of the measurement cycle, scan_2026-10-07_composite_d, at most once in the whole report, where the section says what was measured.
- Do not use Markdown formatting inside sentences: no bold, no italics, no backticks, no bullet lists.

FACTS
- Every fact you state must come from the CLAIMS below. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere, even if you are sure it is true. FRAMING text, if any, tells you what the work is for; it is not a source of facts, and a fact taken from it that no claim states will be cut.
- A sentence that states a fact ends with the ids of the claims that support every part of it, written as [c:CL-035] or [c:CL-035, CL-036], placed before the final full stop. A sentence with no fact in it (a transition, a statement of what the section does) has no marker.
- Write every number exactly as a claim states it, in digits, with its thousands separator (1,055, not 1055 or one thousand and fifty-five). Do not compute a new number (no sums, differences, percentages or ratios that no claim states). A number that is not in a claim the sentence cites will be cut.
- Do not overstate. A claim that says "at most", "a bound, not a value", "notional", "not established" or "candidate" keeps that qualification in your sentence.
- A sentence that the claims do not support will be cut, not repaired, and the argument will have a hole where it was.

Return ONLY a JSON object, with no prose before or after it and no code fence:
{"paragraphs": [["first sentence of paragraph one [c:CL-001].", "second sentence."], ["first sentence of paragraph two."]]}
Each paragraph is a list of its sentences, in order; each sentence is one string.

NAMES (a code in a claim, and the name to write instead)
A12: the check for access policy coherence (An identified, robots-compliant machine client that robots.txt permits is served (not refused by a WAF or bot manager))
A13: the check for discoverability from the product page (A machine client starting from the product page reaches the body's API, its terms, its changelog and its inventory without being told where they are)
B1: the check for variable-level semantics (Comprehensive variable-level metadata (labels, definitions, units, universes))
B2: the check for definitions surface (Concept/term definitions published, versioned, linked from variables)
B4: the check for quality metadata (Data-quality attributes (error measures, suppression rules, revisions policy) published as metadata, not prose)
D3: the check for provenance completeness (Source lineage published (collection → processing → product))
D4: the check for no dark data (Statutory products enumerable from a public inventory (data.gov/agency inventory current))
G4: the check for authority metadata (The issuing authority of a data product is carried as machine-readable metadata on the product's catalog record: in `publisher`, the field DCAT-US 3.0 defines for it (Recommended), or in the agency codes DCAT-US 1.1 requires of federal datasets (`bureauCode`, `programCode`), which DCAT-US 3.0 does not define and does not reject)
